questions.question: What is the purpose of an element filter in Performance Analytics?

options.text: To calculate indicator scores from filtered data
To specify or limit the displayed breakdown elements on visualizations
To define which indicators appear on dashboards
To restrict user access to specific dashboards

explanation.correct: Element filters enable you to specify or limit the displayed breakdown elements on visualizations.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Indicator sources, not element filters, determine which records contribute to indicator scores.
Dashboard configuration determines which indicators appear, not element filters.
Dashboard sharing and roles control user access, not element filters.

source.excerpt: Element filters enable you to specify or limit the displayed breakdown elements on visualizations.

questions.question: Which role is required to create an element filter in Performance Analytics?

explanation.correct: The role pa_data_collector or admin is required to create an element filter.

wrongAnswers.explanation: pa_viewer provides read-only access and cannot create filters.
While pa_power_user has many permissions, pa_data_collector is specifically required for element filters.
pa_contributor allows score entry but not element filter creation.

questions.question: In which two places can element filters be applied in Platform Analytics? (Choose two.)

options.text: KPI Details Filters pane under 'Refine by'
Analytics Hub when selecting a breakdown

explanation.correct: Element filters can be applied on KPI Details under 'Refine by' when selecting a breakdown, and in the Analytics Hub when you select a breakdown that has element filters on its breakdown source.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Data collection jobs don't use element filters; they collect all scores based on indicator sources.
Indicator sources define what data to collect, not how to filter displayed breakdown elements.

source.excerpt: On the Core UI Analytics Hub: When you select a breakdown, if that breakdown has elements filters, you get a list of them to choose from. On KPI Details in Platform Analytics: When you select a breakdown in the Filters pane, if that breakdown has elements filters, you get a list of them to choose from under Refine by.

questions.question: What must be used for personalized visuals with element filters?

options.text: The [equals] operator in the filter condition
The [is (dynamic)] operator in the filter condition

explanation.correct: For Personalized visuals, the operator in the filter condition must be [is (dynamic)].

wrongAnswers.explanation: The standard [equals] operator doesn't support personalization; [is (dynamic)] is required.
Manual breakdown sources are not specifically required for personalized visuals.
Scripted breakdown mappings serve a different purpose than personalized visuals.

source.excerpt: For Personalized visuals, the operator in the filter condition must be [is (dynamic)].

questions.question: How many levels of breakdown can be applied to an indicator in Performance Analytics?

explanation.correct: You cannot apply more than two levels of breakdown to an indicator.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Two levels of breakdown are supported, not just one.
The maximum is two levels, not three.
There is a limit of two breakdown levels per indicator.

source.excerpt: You cannot apply more than two levels of breakdown to an indicator.

questions.question: What happens when you add a filter in Interactive Analysis and click Apply Filters?

options.text: The filter is saved permanently to the indicator
The new filter element appears in the Group by and Stack by lists
A new breakdown source is created automatically
The data collector job runs immediately

explanation.correct: When you add a filter in Interactive Analysis and click Apply Filters, the new filter element appears in the Group by and Stack by lists.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Filters in Interactive Analysis are session-based, not permanently saved to indicators.
Adding filters doesn't create breakdown sources; those are separate configurations.
Filters in Interactive Analysis don't trigger data collection jobs.

source.excerpt: Click Apply Filters. The new filter element appears in the Group by and Stack by lists.

questions.question: Which three types of breakdowns are supported based on where their elements come from? (Choose three.)

explanation.correct: Breakdowns are categorized as automated, manual, or external, depending on where the breakdown elements come from.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Formula applies to indicators, not breakdowns.
Scripted is a type of breakdown mapping, not a breakdown category. Breakdowns can use scripted mappings but are still categorized as automated/manual/external.

source.excerpt: Breakdowns are categorized as automated, manual, or external, depending on where these elements come from.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a breakdown mapping in Performance Analytics?

options.text: To define the visual appearance of breakdowns on dashboards
To specify relationships between breakdowns and indicator sources
To schedule when breakdown data is collected
To determine which users can view breakdown data

explanation.correct: Breakdown mappings specify the relationships, or 'map,' breakdowns to indicator sources. A breakdown mapping either specifies a field on the indicator source or specifies a script that queries the indicator source.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Visual appearance is controlled by widget and dashboard configuration, not breakdown mappings.
Data collection scheduling is done through data collector jobs, not breakdown mappings.
User access is controlled by roles and dashboard sharing, not breakdown mappings.

source.excerpt: Breakdown mappings specify the relationships, or 'map,' breakdowns to indicator sources.

questions.question: What is a bucket group used for in Performance Analytics breakdowns?

options.text: To group indicator scores by time period
To recategorize data by grouping values into discrete buckets
To limit dashboard access by user groups

explanation.correct: Bucket groups are used to recategorize data so it can be used as a breakdown, for example by grouping a range of values into discrete buckets.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Time period grouping is done through indicator frequency settings, not bucket groups.
Historical data is stored in the Scores table, not bucket groups.
Dashboard access is controlled by sharing settings, not bucket groups.

source.excerpt: Bucket groups are used to recategorize data so it can be used as a breakdown, for example by grouping a range of values into discrete buckets.

questions.question: An administrator wants to create an element filter that shows only users in the HR department from the User [sys_user] breakdown source. What should they configure in the Filter field?

explanation.correct: For example, if the breakdown source facts table is User [sys_user], you can add a filter condition to include only users in the HR department with [Department][is][HR].

wrongAnswers.explanation: Name contains would filter by user name, not department membership.
Group is a different field from Department in the User table.
User Type is not the correct field for filtering by department.

source.excerpt: For example, if the breakdown source facts table is User [sys_user], you can add a filter condition to include only users in the HR department. This filter condition is [Department][is][HR].

questions.question: Which table is used as the facts table when creating a breakdown source that uses bucket groups?

explanation.correct: To work with a bucket group, create a breakdown source that uses Bucket [pa_buckets] as the facts table and specifies the bucket group in a condition.

wrongAnswers.explanation: PA Scores stores indicator score data, not bucket group definitions.
Breakdown Element stores individual elements, not bucket group configurations.
Indicator Source defines data for indicators, not bucket group breakdowns.

source.excerpt: To work with a bucket group, create a breakdown source that uses Bucket [pa_buckets] as the facts table and specifies the bucket group in a condition.

questions.question: What is the result of setting a Default element filter on a breakdown record?

options.text: The filter becomes the only filter available for that breakdown
The filter is selected automatically for that breakdown in any visualization
The filter is applied permanently and cannot be changed
The filter is copied to all existing dashboards

explanation.correct: You can specify a Default element filter on a breakdown record. That elements filter is selected automatically for that breakdown in any visualization. Users that view the breakdown on the Analytics Hub or on KPI Details can change or clear the selected elements filter.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Other filters remain available; the default is just pre-selected.
Users can change or clear the default filter when viewing.
Default filters are not copied to dashboards; they're applied dynamically.

source.excerpt: Besides specifying an elements filter on a visualization, you can specify a Default element filter on a breakdown record. That elements filter is selected automatically for that breakdown in any visualization. Users that view the breakdown on the Analytics Hub or on KPI Details can change or clear the selected elements filter.

questions.question: What does the PAFormulaUtils method getCurrentBreakdownLevel2ID() return?

options.text: The level 2 breakdown identifier (sys_id) from the current formula indicator
The count of breakdown elements at level 2

explanation.correct: getCurrentBreakdownLevel2ID() returns the level 2 breakdown identifier (sys_id) from the indicator of the current formula. The sys_id is returned dynamically as the selection in the Analytics Hub changes.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The method returns a sys_id, not a name, and specifically for level 2.
This method returns the breakdown ID, not a count of elements.
This returns the breakdown ID, not the breakdown source ID.

source.excerpt: Returns the level 2 breakdown identifier (sys_id) from the indicator of the current formula. The sys_id is returned dynamically, as the selection in the Analytics Hub changes.

questions.question: Which widget types in Core UI support the use of element filters?

options.text: Breakdown, time series, and score widgets

explanation.correct: Only breakdown, time series, and score widgets support elements filters. For time series and score widgets, an elements filter replaces the first-level breakdown element. For breakdown widgets, an elements filter limits the elements that are shown.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Time series and score widgets also support element filters.
Not all widgets support element filters; only breakdown, time series, and score widgets do.
Breakdown and score widgets also support element filters.

source.excerpt: Only breakdown, time series, and score widgets support elements filters. For time series and score widgets, an elements filter replaces the first-level breakdown element. For breakdown widgets, an elements filter limits the elements that are shown.

questions.question: An administrator creates an element filter on the Groups breakdown source and wants to show only groups that had an incident assigned to them in the last 6 months. Which filter type should they use?

explanation.correct: Use RELATED LIST CONDITIONS to include a relationship with another table. For example, creating an element filter on the Groups breakdown source with a related list condition on Incident->Assignment group and Created in Last 6 Months would show only groups assigned incidents in that timeframe.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Standard CONDITIONS filter on the same table, not related tables.
A scripted filter is not needed; RELATED LIST CONDITIONS handles this scenario.
Time-based filter is not a specific filter type; use RELATED LIST CONDITIONS with time criteria.

source.excerpt: RELATED LIST CONDITIONS: Include a relationship with another table in the conditions. For example, you could create an element filter on the Groups breakdown source, which uses the Group [sys_user_group] table. If you added a related list condition on Incident [incident]->Assignment group, you would get only groups that had an incident assigned to them.
